purpose: The platform line's first decline after two years of steep growth: 689.9m -> 2,607.7m -> 3,897.5m · > 5,585.9m (FY2025/26 Supp I) -> **3,612.6m proposed for FY2026/27** - still 5x its June-2024 · size, but the surge has crested. Projections hold flat (~3.65bn).

The identity series' third year: 6,836.3m (FY2024/25) -> 8,085.6m (FY2025/26, then 11,074.0m at · Supp I) -> 10,993.0m proposed. NRB holds near its supplementary peak; the baseline column of this · PBB also recovers the FY2025/26 Supp I programme and vote totals that row-wrap obscured (Pop Mgmt · 11,073,992,261; Vote 1024 total 29,262,215,179).

The vote was **restructured**: the Konza/BPO capital-transfer line disappears (its successor, ICT · Technical Support Services, carries 150m), E-Government splits into four function-named · sub-programmes, and a wholly new programme 0222000 puts cyber and data protection on their own · lines. Budget-day thematic: KSh 8.6bn "digital superhighway and creative economy" - the second · consecutive cut (16.3bn -> 12.7bn -> 8.6bn) - with KSh 4.3bn of it the World Bank-backed KDEAP · (externally financed - excluded from domestic-state totals at the origin gate; definite-match to · the held KDEAP deal record at full extract). **No Konza DC/KAIST allocation was disclosed at · budget day** (Business Daily, 2026-06-11) - not established whether it moved votes or ended.
notes: (appropriated)* Baseline column = FY2025/26 Supp I values exactly, corroborating that Supp II left Vote 1122 · unamended (the KEN/2025 flag) - the FY2025/26 annual BIRR still settles it verbatim.
